title: Einstein & AI in Data 360

toc.text: 2. Generative AI on Data 360: the RAG stack
4. AI in the flow of customer 360

html:
AI is the reason Data 360 exists as an agentic data layer: unified data feeds predictions and generative AI across the platform. This phase covers Einstein Studio, predictive modeling on DMOs, generative grounding, and how Data 360 becomes the context engine for Einstein Copilot and Agentforce (deep detail in Phase 14).

Learning Objectives

By the end of this phase, you will be able to:

  • Position Einstein Studio (models/BYOM) and Data 360's predictive capabilities.
  • Scope a predictive use case (churn, LTV, propensity) from unified-profile features.
  • Explain RAG on Data 360: indexing, embedding, retrievers, and hybrid search.
  • Describe how prompt templates get Data 360 merge fields and retrievers.
  • Know the AI governance guardrails (grounding, PII, audit) expected of a Data 360 consultant.

1. Predictive AI: Einstein Studio

Einstein Studio is the maker workspace for Data 360 AI: build models over DMO/unified-profile data, train them, and deploy a predicted score back onto profiles (a Predicted_... attribute) and segments.

  • Model types — propensity (will buy), churn (will churn), LTV, next-best-action; formulated as binary or regression targets.
  • Features — the DMO attributes that predict the target (spend, frequency, tenure, engagement).
  • Output — predictions deployed as profile attributes consumed by segments, journeys, and flows ("send win-back to Predicted_Churn >= 0.65").
  • BYOM (bring your own model) — import external model output so a single unified profile also carries your team's scores.

The consultation pattern: define the business decision first, then the target & features, then the deployment point. A churn model is useless if no segment/activation consumes the score.

2. Generative AI on Data 360: the RAG stack

Large-volume unstructured+structured grounding is Data 360's superpower. The components you must map:

ComponentRole
Indexing & chunkingData 360 ingests files/Knowledge/PDFs into searchable chunks (metadata-indexed).
EmbeddingsVectors for semantic similarity (native vector database).
RetrieversNo-code configs that fetch the most relevant chunks for a query, with filters/ranking.
Hybrid searchVector (semantic) + keyword (exact) retrieval — mandatory for domain terms (SKUs, product codes).
GroundingRetrieved context is included in the prompt so the LLM answers from facts, not guesses.

The "is this grounded?" question is the exam's favourite guardrail: an answer that doesn't cite/grok retrieved context is hallucination risk. Prompt templates (below) make grounding structural.

3. Prompt Builder + Data 360

Prompt Builder templates become Prompt Templates (agent actions) and flow steps. Data 360 integration points:

  1. Merge fields — insert unified-profile fields into the prompt ({{!$DataCloud....}}-style, or standard merge fields fed by retrieved context).
  2. Retriever reference — a template can attach a Data 360/no-code retriever so answers come with supporting context.
  3. Model choice — route to gpt/open models; governance layer applies PII masking and audit.

The recommended pattern for a service agent: an "Answer with Case Data" agent action built on a prompt template whose retriever is scoped to the Knowledge/DMO context — the exact hands-on the Trailhead "grounded service agent" trail demonstrates.

4. AI in the flow of customer 360

Where AI touches the data layer every day:

  • Einstein for Service (case classification, resolution insights) — grounded on unified case data.
  • Einstein Sales (propensity) — prediction attributes over recent unified activity.
  • Agentforce — the crown consumer: agents reason on Data Graphs (Phase 14) built from DMOs and retrieval context.
  • Data 360 Copilot/Assistant — natural-language querying of your data assets.

Consultant discipline: every AI feature is only as good as — and only as trusted as — the governance around it. Plan the audit + PII masking + feedback logging alongside the model, and get consent/PII decisions signed off before go-live.

5. Lab tie-in

The repo's Apex can't train models, but EinsteinRecommendationService (incoming in Phase 16/17 exercises) mirrors the consumption pattern: scoring records against a persisted model output field and feeding those scores into the flow/trigger chain — the same wiring a deployed Predicted_Churn__c attribute uses inside service automation.

Hands-On Exercises

Exercise 1: Model spec

Write the spec for a "Likely-to-repeat-customer" model: business decision, target (binary/regression? horizon?), candidate features (4), training data source (which DMO), and deployment attribute (field + where consumed).

Exercise 2: RAG reader

Given an agent that must answer "why did my order 5821 refund?", lay out the grounding sources (order DMO, case/transaction data, Knowledge), the retriever filter, and why hybrid search matters for 5821.

Exercise 3: Review a prompt template

Draft a prompt template for the refund scenario with: system tone, the merge fields from the unified profile, the retriever input, and a "if insufficient context, say so" instruction. Note what the governance layer masks.

Key Terms Glossary

TermDefinition
Einstein StudioData 360 workspace to build/deploy predictive models over DMOs.
Prediction attributeDeployed model score on the unified profile (e.g. Predicted_Churn).
BYOMBring Your Own Model output imported onto profiles.
RetrieverConfig that fetches relevant context for grounding a prompt.
Hybrid searchVector + keyword retrieval combined.
RAGRetrieval-Augmented Generation — grounding LLM answers in retrieved facts.
Prompt Builder / Prompt TemplateTool/artifact that defines structured prompts with merge fields and retrievers.
GroundingThe practice of binding a generated answer to trusted, retrieved context.

Certification Checkpoints

  • I can write a predictive use-case spec (decision → target → features → deployment).
  • I can place Einstein Studio and BYOM in the Data 360 AI stack.
  • I can explain RAG components (indexing, embeddings, retriever, hybrid search).
  • I can build a prompt template grounded in Data 360 context with governance.
  • I can defend the governance plan (PII masking, audit, feedback) for an AI feature.

Self-Check

  1. Q: Which artifact feeds a segment from a model? — A: The model's prediction attribute deployed onto unified profiles; segments then filter on that score.
  2. Q: Why hybrid search for an order-number query? — A: Keyword exact-match finds 5821; vector search alone may not match a literal SKU/order number.
  3. Q: What makes an agent answer "grounded"? — A: Retrieved context is injected into the prompt and the template instructs the model to answer from that context (with "insufficient context" fallback).
